translations.literal: Taichang year 1, tenth month, day dingmao: disaster at the Huiluan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Taichang 1, tenth month, dingmao: the Huiluan Palace burned.

sentences.zh: 天啓元年閏二月丙戌，昭和殿災。

translations.literal: Tianqi year 1, intercalary second month, day bingxu: disaster at Zhaohua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 1, intercalary second month, bingxu: Zhaohua Hall burned.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，杭州火，延燒六千餘家。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiachen: fire at Hangzhou spread to burn more than six thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, jiachen: fire at Hangzhou spread to consume more than six thousand households.

sentences.zh: 八月戊子，復災，城內外延毀萬餘家。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day wuzi: burned again; within and beyond the walls more than ten thousand households destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, wuzi: fire struck again; within and beyond the walls more than ten thousand households were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 二年五月丙申，旗纛廟正殿災，火藥盡焚，匠役多死者。

translations.literal: Year 2, fifth month, day bingshen: disaster at the main hall of the Banner and Pennant Temple; gunpowder all burned; many craftsmen and laborers died.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 2, fifth month, bingshen: the main hall of the Banner and Pennant Temple burned; gunpowder was all consumed and many craftsmen and laborers died.

sentences.zh: 三年七月辛卯，南京大內左傍宮災。

translations.literal: Year 3, seventh month, day xinmao: disaster at the left-side palace beside the Nanjing inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 3, seventh month, xinmao: the left-side palace beside the Nanjing inner palace burned.

sentences.zh: 六年五月戊申，王恭廠災，地中霹靂聲不絕，火藥自焚，煙塵障空，白晝晦冥，凡四五里。

translations.literal: Year 6, fifth month, day wushen: disaster at the Wanggong Works; thunderclaps in the ground unceasing; gunpowder burned of itself; dust and smoke blocked the sky; broad daylight turned dim; for four or five li.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 6, fifth month, wushen: disaster at the Wanggong Works; thunderclaps rolled unceasing from underground as gunpowder ignited of itself; dust and smoke blocked the sky until broad daylight turned dim for four or five li.

sentences.zh: 五月癸亥，朝天宮災。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day guihai: disaster at Chaotian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, guihai: Chaotian Palace burned.

sentences.zh: 七月庚寅，登州城樓火。

translations.literal: Seventh month, day gengyin: fire at the Dengzhou city tower.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, gengyin: the Dengzhou city tower burned.

sentences.zh: 七年十月庚子，寧遠前屯火，傷男婦二百餘人。

translations.literal: Year 7, tenth month, day gengzi: fire at Qiantun before Ningyuan; more than two hundred men and women injured.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 7, tenth month, gengzi: fire at Qiantun before Ningyuan injured more than two hundred men and women.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年四月乙卯，左軍都督府災。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 1, fourth month, day yimao: disaster at the Left Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 1, fourth month, yimao: the Left Military Commission burned.

sentences.zh: 五月乙亥，鷹坊司火。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day yihai: fire at the Hawk Works Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, yihai: the Hawk Works Directorate burned.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，丁字庫火。

translations.literal: Day dinghai: fire at the Dingzi Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Dinghai: the Dingzi Storehouse burned.

sentences.zh: 七月己卯，公安縣火，毀文廟，延五千餘家。

translations.literal: Seventh month, day jimao: fire at Gong'an county destroyed the Confucian temple and spread to five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, jimao: fire at Gong'an county destroyed the Confucian temple and spread to more than five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月庚子，火藥局災。

translations.literal: Year 2, eleventh month, day gengzi: disaster at the Gunpowder Office.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 2, eleventh month, gengzi: the Gunpowder Office burned.

sentences.zh: 三年三月戊戌，又災。

translations.literal: Year 3, third month, day wuxu: burned again.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 3, third month, wuxu: it burned again.

sentences.zh: 八月癸酉，頭道關災，火器轟擊無餘。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day guiyou: disaster at the First Pass; firearms exploded until nothing remained.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, guiyou: disaster at the First Pass; firearms detonated until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 六年正月癸丑，濟南舜廟災。

translations.literal: Year 6, first month, day guichou: disaster at the Shun Temple in Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 6, first month, guichou: the Shun Temple in Jinan burned.

sentences.zh: 七年九月庚申，盔甲廠災。

translations.literal: Year 7, ninth month, day gengshen: disaster at the Armor Factory.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 7, ninth month, gengshen: the Armor Factory burned.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月戊戌，新火藥局災。

translations.literal: Year 11, fourth month, day wuxu: disaster at the New Gunpowder Office.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 11, fourth month, wuxu: the New Gunpowder Office burned.

sentences.zh: 傷人甚衆。

translations.literal: Very many persons were injured.
translations.idiomatic: Very many people were injured.

sentences.zh: 六月癸巳，安民廠災，震毀城垣廨舍，居民死傷無算。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day guisi: disaster at the Anmin Works; the shock destroyed city walls and government offices; among residents dead and injured beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, guisi: disaster at the Anmin Works; the blast wrecked city walls and government offices, and among the residents the dead and injured were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 八月丁酉，火藥局又災。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day dingyou: the Gunpowder Office burned again.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, dingyou: the Gunpowder Office burned again.

sentences.zh: ▲火異

translations.literal: ▲ Fire anomalies
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Fire Anomalies

sentences.zh: 成化二十一年正月甲申朔，有火光自中天而少西，墜於下，化爲白氣，復曲折上騰，聲如雷。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 21, first month, first day of the month jiashen: there was fire-light from mid-heaven slightly westward; it fell below, turned into white vapor, then wound upward again; sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 21, first month, first day jiashen: a blaze of light appeared in mid-heaven slightly to the west, fell below and turned into white vapor, then wound upward again with a sound like thunder.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年三月庚午，儀隴空中有紅白火焰，長三丈餘，自縣治東北流，至正東六十餘里而墜，聲震如雷。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 3, third month, day gengwu: in the sky over Yilong there were red and white flames three zhang long; they flowed from northeast of the county seat to due east for more than sixty li and fell; sound shook like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 3, third month, gengwu: red and white flames more than three zhang long appeared in the sky over Yilong, flowed from northeast of the county seat to due east for more than sixty li, and fell with a thunderous roar.

sentences.zh: 八年三月辛卯，廣寧右衛臺杆火，高五寸，杆如故。

translations.literal: Year 8, third month, day xinmao: fire at a beacon pole of Guangning Right Guard; five cun high; the pole remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8, third month, xinmao: fire appeared on a beacon pole of Guangning Right Guard five cun high; the pole itself was unharmed.

sentences.zh: 十年四月辛丑，阜平有火光，長八九尺，大如轆軸，有聲，自東南至西南而墜。

translations.literal: Year 10, fourth month, day xinchou: at Fuping there was fire-light eight or nine chi long, large as a windlass drum, with sound; it fell from southeast to southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 10, fourth month, xinchou: at Fuping fire-light eight or nine chi long and large as a windlass drum, with sound, fell from southeast to southwest.

sentences.zh: 正德元年三月戊申夜，太原有火如斗大，墜寧化王殿前。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 1, third month, night of day wushen: at Taiyuan there was fire like a dou in size; it fell before the hall of the Prince of Ninghua.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 1, third month, night of wushen: at Taiyuan fire the size of a dou fell before the hall of the Prince of Ninghua.

sentences.zh: 廣寧墩臺火發旗杆，凡六。

translations.literal: At Guangning beacon platforms fire broke out on flagpoles; six in all.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangning beacon platforms fire broke out on flagpoles; six in all.

sentences.zh: 七月壬戌夜，火光墜即墨民家，化爲綠石，圓高尺餘。

translations.literal: Seventh month, night of day renxu: fire-light fell on a civilian house in Jimo and turned into green stone, round, more than a chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, night of renxu: fire-light fell on a civilian house in Jimo and turned into green stone, round and more than a chi high.

sentences.zh: 七年三月丁卯夜，大風雷電，餘干仙居寨有光如箭，墜旗竿上，俄如燭龍，光照四野。

translations.literal: Year 7, third month, night of day dingmao: great wind, thunder, and lightning; at Yugan Xianju Stockade there was light like an arrow; it fell on a flagpole, soon like the Candle Dragon, its light illuminating the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 7, third month, night of dingmao: amid great wind, thunder, and lightning, at Yugan Xianju Stockade light like an arrow fell on a flagpole and soon blazed like the Candle Dragon, illuminating the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 士卒撼其旗，飛上竿首，既而其火四散，槍首皆有光如星。

translations.literal: Soldiers shook the flag; it flew to the top of the pole; then its fire scattered in four directions; spear tips all had light like stars.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers shook the flag; it flew to the top of the pole; then its fire scattered in four directions, and every spear tip bore star-like light.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月己亥夜，火隕都察院獄，旋轉久之始滅。

translations.literal: Year 12, fifth month, night of day jihai: fire fell at the Censorate prison; it revolved a long while before extinguishing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 12, fifth month, night of jihai: fire fell at the Censorate prison and revolved a long while before it went out.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月癸未夜，台州火隕三，大如盤，觸草木皆焦。

translations.literal: Year 15, sixth month, night of day guiwei: three fires fell at Taizhou, large as platters; whatever plants they touched were scorched.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 15, sixth month, night of guiwei: three fires fell at Taizhou, large as platters; whatever plants they touched were scorched.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年七月甲申，有火球三，大五六尺，從北墜於東，其光燭天。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 5, seventh month, day jiashen: there were three fire-balls five or six chi in size; they fell from the north toward the east; their light lit the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 5, seventh month, jiashen: three fire-balls five or six chi across fell from the north toward the east, their light lighting the sky.

sentences.zh: 二十年七月丙戌，火球如鬥，隕左軍都督府中門東，良久乃滅。

translations.literal: Year 20, seventh month, day bingxu: a fire-ball like a dou fell east of the middle gate of the Left Military Commission; after a long while it went out.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 20, seventh month, bingxu: a fire-ball the size of a dou fell east of the middle gate of the Left Military Commission and after a long while went out.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年三月戊午，延綏保寧堡城角旗杆出火，灼灼有聲。

translations.literal: Longqing year 2, third month, day wuwu: at Yan'an Baoning Fort the corner flagpole of the city wall emitted fire, blazing with sound.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing 2, third month, wuwu: at Yan'an Baoning Fort the corner flagpole of the city wall emitted blazing fire with sound.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十四年，保定府民間牆壁內出火，三日夜乃熄。

translations.literal: Wanli year 14: fire issued from within civilian house walls in Baoding prefecture; after three days and nights it went out.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 14: fire issued from within civilian house walls in Baoding prefecture and went out only after three days and nights.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，綏靖邊城各堡，脊獸旗杆俱出火。

translations.literal: Year 15, second month: at Suijing and border forts, ridge beasts and flagpoles all emitted fire.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 15, second month: at Suijing and the border forts, ridge beasts and flagpoles all emitted fire.

sentences.zh: 軍士以杖撲之，杖亦生火，三更乃熄。

translations.literal: Soldiers beat them with staves; the staves also caught fire; at the third watch it went out.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers beat them with staves; the staves also caught fire; at the third watch it went out.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，陝西空中有火，大如盆，後生三尾，隕於西北。

translations.literal: Year 20, third month: in the sky over Shaanxi there was fire large as a basin; afterward three tails grew; it fell in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 20, third month: in the sky over Shaanxi there was fire large as a basin; afterward three tails grew, and it fell in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 二十一年二月庚辰夜分，大毛山樓上各獸吻俱有火，如雞卵，赤色，即時雨雪，火上嗟嗟有聲。

translations.literal: Year 21, second month, night of day gengchen: on the tower of Great Mao Mountain each beast finial had fire like a chicken egg, red in color; at once rain and snow fell; on the fire there was a sizzling sound.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 21, second month, night of gengchen: on the tower of Great Mao Mountain each beast finial bore fire like a red chicken egg; at once rain and snow fell, and the flames sizzled audibly.

sentences.zh: 二十三年九月癸巳夜，永寧有火光，形如屋大，隕於西北。

translations.literal: Year 23, ninth month, night of day guisi: at Yongning there was fire light, shaped like a house in size, falling in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 23, ninth month, night of day guisi: at Yongning fire light the size of a house fell in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 永昌、鎮番、寧遠所見同。

translations.literal: Yongchang, Zhenfan, and Ningyuan saw the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same phenomenon was seen at Yongchang, Zhenfan, and Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 二十四年二月戊申夜，鄠縣雷雨，遍地火光，十有餘里。

translations.literal: Year 24, second month, night of day wushen: at Hu County thunder and rain; fire light spread over the ground for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 24, second month, night of day wushen: thunder and rain struck Hu County, and fire light spread across the ground for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 二十五年二月癸亥，平涼瓦獸口出火，水灌不滅。

translations.literal: Year 25, second month, day guihai: at Pingliang the mouths of the roof-tile beasts emitted fire; water poured on them would not extinguish it.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 25, second month, day guihai: at Pingliang the mouths of the ceramic roof-beast ornaments emitted fire that could not be quenched even when water was poured on them.

sentences.zh: 八月甲申，肅、涼二州火光在天，形如車輪，尾分三股，約長三丈。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day jiashen: at Su and Liang two prefectures fire light was in the sky, shaped like a carriage wheel; its tail split into three strands, about three zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, day jiashen: at Su and Liang prefectures fire light appeared in the sky shaped like a carriage wheel, its tail splitting into three strands about three zhang long.

sentences.zh: 天啓六年五月壬寅朔，厚載門火神廟紅球滾出，前門城樓角有數千螢火，併合如車輪。

translations.literal: Tianqi year 6, fifth month, new moon of day renyin: at the Houzai Gate Fire God Temple a red ball rolled out; at the corner of the front gate tower were several thousand fireflies, merging like a carriage wheel.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 6, fifth month, new moon of day renyin: at the Houzai Gate Fire God Temple a red ball rolled out, and at the corner of the front gate tower several thousand fireflies merged into a shape like a carriage wheel.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，西安有火如碾如鬥者數十，色青，焰高尺許，嘗入民居，留數日乃去。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 1: at Xi'an there were several tens of fires like millstones and like dippers, blue in color, flames a chi or more high; they sometimes entered commoners' dwellings and after several days then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 1: at Xi'an several dozen fires shaped like millstones and dippers appeared, blue in color with flames a chi or more high; they sometimes entered private homes and lingered for days before departing.

sentences.zh: 用羊豕禳之，不爲害，自五月至七月而止。

translations.literal: Sheep and pigs were used to avert it; it did no harm, and from the fifth month to the seventh month it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep and pigs were offered to avert the omen; it did no harm, and from the fifth month to the seventh month it ceased.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月壬申，鎮安火光如斛，自西墜地，士木皆焦。

translations.literal: Year 13, sixth month, day renshen: at Zhen'an fire light like a hu fell from the west to the ground; earth and wood were all scorched.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 13, sixth month, day renshen: at Zhen'an fire light the size of a hu fell from the west to the ground, scorching earth and timber alike.

sentences.zh: ▲赤眚赤祥

translations.literal: ▲ Red afflictions and red omens.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Red Afflictions and Red Omens

sentences.zh: 成化十三年二月甲午，浙江山陰涌泉如血。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 13, second month, day jiawu: at Shanyin in Zhejiang a spring gushed blood like blood.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 13, second month, day jiawu: at Shanyin in Zhejiang a spring gushed blood.

sentences.zh: 正德元年正月乙酉夜，崇明空中有紅光，曳尾如虹，起東北至西南沒，聲如雷。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 1, first month, night of day yiyou: in the sky at Chongming there was red light, trailing its tail like a rainbow, rising from the northeast to the southwest and vanishing, with sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 1, first month, night of day yiyou: red light trailed like a rainbow across the sky at Chongming, rising from the northeast to the southwest before vanishing with a sound like thunder.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，鳳陽紅光發，與日同色，聲如雷。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: at Fengyang red light issued forth, the same color as the sun, with sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinchou: at Fengyang red light burst forth the same color as the sun, with a sound like thunder.

sentences.zh: 二年八月己亥，赤光見寧夏，長五丈。

translations.literal: Year 2, eighth month, day jihai: red light appeared at Ningxia, five zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 2, eighth month, day jihai: red light appeared at Ningxia, five zhang long.

sentences.zh: 八年七月甲申，龍泉有赤彈二，自空隕於縣治，形如鵝卵，躍入民居，相鬥久之。

translations.literal: Year 8, seventh month, day jiashen: at Longquan there were two red balls, falling from the sky at the county seat, shaped like goose eggs; they leaped into commoners' dwellings and fought one another for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 8, seventh month, day jiashen: at Longquan two red balls fell from the sky at the county seat, shaped like goose eggs; they leaped into private homes and fought one another for a long while.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十三年四月戊子，慈溪民家涌血高尺餘。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 33, fourth month, day wuzi: at a commoner's house in Cixi blood gushed more than a chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 33, fourth month, day wuzi: at a commoner's house in Cixi blood gushed more than a chi high.

sentences.zh: 三十七年五月戊辰，東陽民張思齊家地裂五六處，出血如線，高尺許。

translations.literal: Year 37, fifth month, day wuchen: at Dongyang commoner Zhang Siqi's house the ground split in five or six places and blood issued like threads, a chi or more high.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 37, fifth month, day wuchen: at Dongyang the ground at commoner Zhang Siqi's house split in five or six places and blood issued in threads a chi or more high.

sentences.zh: 血凝，犬就食之，掘地無所見。

translations.literal: The blood congealed; a dog went and ate it; digging in the ground nothing was seen.
translations.idiomatic: The blood congealed; a dog came and ate it, yet digging in the ground revealed nothing.

sentences.zh: 三十九年二月己未，竹溪民家出血。

translations.literal: Year 39, second month, day jiwei: at a commoner's house in Zhuxi blood issued forth.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 39, second month, day jiwei: blood issued forth at a commoner's house in Zhuxi.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年閏二月癸酉，遼東赤風揚塵蔽天。

translations.literal: Longqing year 6, intercalary second month, day guiyou: in Liaodong a red wind raised dust and blotted out the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing 6, intercalary second month, day guiyou: in Liaodong a red wind raised dust and blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年七月丁丑，鬆門衛金鐺家涌血三尺，有聲。

translations.literal: Wanli year 6, seventh month, day dingchou: at the Jindang household in Songmen Guard blood gushed three chi, with sound.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 6, seventh month, day dingchou: at the Jindang household in Songmen Guard blood gushed three chi high, with sound.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月乙丑，虹民王祿投宿姚壘家，見血出於地，驚走至市，市亦流血。

translations.literal: Year 13, fourth month, day yichou: the Hong commoner Wang Lu lodged at Yao Lei's house and saw blood issue from the ground; startled, he ran to the market, and the market too bled.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 13, fourth month, day yichou: the Hong commoner Wang Lu lodged at Yao Lei's house and saw blood issue from the ground; startled, he ran to the market, and the market too bled.

sentences.zh: 鄉人擊器物噪之，乃止。

translations.literal: Villagers struck vessels and made noise; only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers struck vessels and raised a clamor; only then did it stop.

sentences.zh: 十九年六月庚戌，慈溪茅家浦涌血八處，大如盆，高尺許。

translations.literal: Year 19, sixth month, day gengxu: at Maojiapu in Cixi blood gushed in eight places, large as basins and a chi or more high.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 19, sixth month, day gengxu: at Maojiapu in Cixi blood gushed in eight places, as large as basins and a chi or more high.

sentences.zh: 血濺船，船即出血，濺人足，足亦出血，數刻乃絕。

translations.literal: Blood splashed a boat, and the boat too issued blood; it splashed a man's foot, and the foot too issued blood; after several quarters of an hour it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Blood splashed a boat, and the boat too issued blood; it splashed a man's foot, and the foot too issued blood; after several quarters of an hour it ceased.

sentences.zh: 二十六年九月甲辰，蕭山賈九經家出血，高尺許。

translations.literal: Year 26, ninth month, day jiachen: at the household of Jia Jiujing in Xiaoshan blood issued forth, a chi or more high.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 26, ninth month, day jiachen: at the household of Jia Jiujing in Xiaoshan blood issued forth a chi or more high.

sentences.zh: 天啓元年六月庚寅，肇慶民王體積中庭噴血，如跑突泉。

translations.literal: Tianqi year 1, sixth month, day gengyin: at Zhaoqing commoner Wang Tiji's central courtyard sprayed blood like the Paotu Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 1, sixth month, day gengyin: at Zhaoqing commoner Wang Tiji's central courtyard sprayed blood like the Paotu Spring.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年二月戊午，海豐雨血。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 7, second month, day wuwu: at Haifeng it rained blood.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 7, second month, day wuwu: at Haifeng it rained blood.

sentences.zh: 八年八月戊寅，宣城池中出血。

translations.literal: Year 8, eighth month, day wuyin: within Xuancheng city blood issued forth.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 8, eighth month, day wuyin: blood issued forth within Xuancheng city.

sentences.zh: 《洪範》曰：「木曰曲直。

translations.literal: The Hong Fan says: "Wood is called curve and straight.
translations.idiomatic: The Hong Fan states: "Wood is defined as curve and straight."

sentences.zh: 」木不曲直，則失其性矣。

translations.literal: " When wood is not curve and straight, it loses its nature.
translations.idiomatic: When wood fails to bend and stand straight, it has forsaken its proper nature.

sentences.zh: 前史多以恆雨、狂人、服妖、雞禍、鼠孽、木冰、木妖、青眚青祥皆屬之木，今從之。

translations.literal: Earlier histories mostly classified incessant rain, madmen, eccentric dress, chicken portents, rat calamities, tree ice, tree anomalies, and green afflictions and green omens under wood; this follows them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynastic histories grouped incessant rain, madmen, portentous dress, chicken omens, rat calamities, tree ice, tree anomalies, and green afflictions and green auspices under the element Wood; this chapter follows that convention.

sentences.zh: ▲恆雨

translations.literal: ▲ Incessant rain.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Incessant Rain

sentences.zh: 洪武十三年七月，海康大雨，壞縣治。

translations.literal: Hongwu year 13, seventh month: at Haikang great rain damaged the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 13, seventh month: great rain at Haikang damaged the county seat.

sentences.zh: 二十三年十一月，山東二十九州縣久雨，傷麥禾。

translations.literal: Year 23, eleventh month: in Shandong twenty-nine prefectures and counties prolonged rain harmed wheat and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 23, eleventh month: prolonged rain in twenty-nine prefectures and counties of Shandong harmed wheat and grain.

sentences.zh: 九月，久雨壞密雲中衛城。

translations.literal: Ninth month: prolonged rain damaged the city of Miyun Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: prolonged rain damaged the city of Miyun Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年五月，永嘉、樂清颶風急雨，壞公私廨宇及壇廟。

translations.literal: Xuande year 1, fifth month: at Yongjia and Yueqing hurricane and violent rain damaged public and private offices and altars and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande 1, fifth month: hurricane and violent rain at Yongjia and Yueqing damaged public and private offices and altars and temples.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年，永平、兗州久雨傷禾。

translations.literal: Jingtai year 3: at Yongping and Yanzhou prolonged rain harmed grain.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 3: prolonged rain at Yongping and Yanzhou harmed the grain crop.

sentences.zh: 大嵩等二十衛所久雨壞城。

translations.literal: At Dasong and twenty guards and posts prolonged rain damaged cities.
translations.idiomatic: At Dasong and twenty guards and posts prolonged rain damaged the cities.

sentences.zh: 四年，南畿、河南、山東府十州一，自五月至於八月霪雨傷稼。

translations.literal: Year 4: in the southern metropolitan region, Henan, and Shandong, eleven prefectures and one department, from the fifth month to the eighth month incessant rain harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 4: in the southern metropolitan region, Henan, and Shandong—eleven prefectures and one department—from the fifth month to the eighth month incessant rain harmed the crops.

sentences.zh: 五年，杭、嘉、湖大雨傷苗，六旬不止。

translations.literal: Year 5: at Hang, Jia, and Hu great rain harmed seedlings; for sixty days it did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 5: great rain at Hang, Jia, and Hu harmed seedlings and did not stop for sixty days.

sentences.zh: 七月，京師久雨，九門城垣多壞。

translations.literal: Seventh month: at the capital prolonged rain; many of the Nine Gates city walls were damaged.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: prolonged rain at the capital damaged many of the Nine Gates city walls.

sentences.zh: 六年，北畿府五、河南府二久雨傷稼，雲南大理諸府如之。

translations.literal: Year 6: in the northern metropolitan region five prefectures and Henan two prefectures prolonged rain harmed crops; in Yunnan Dali and various prefectures it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 6: prolonged rain in five prefectures of the northern metropolitan region and two prefectures of Henan harmed crops; Dali and other prefectures in Yunnan suffered likewise.

sentences.zh: 七年，兩畿、江西、河南、浙江、山東、山西、湖廣共府三十，恆雨淹田。

translations.literal: Year 7: in the two metropolitan regions, Jiangxi, Henan, Zhejiang, Shandong, Shanxi, and Huguang, thirty prefectures in all, incessant rain flooded fields.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 7: incessant rain flooded fields in thirty prefectures across the two metropolitan regions, Jiangxi, Henan, Zhejiang, Shandong, Shanxi, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 天順元年，濟、兗、青三府大雨閱月，禾盡沒。

translations.literal: Tianshun year 1: at Ji, Yan, and Qing three prefectures great rain lasted a month; grain was entirely submerged.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 1: at Ji, Yan, and Qing prefectures great rain lasted a month and grain was entirely submerged.

sentences.zh: 四年，安慶、南陽雨，自五月至七月，淹禾苗。

translations.literal: Year 4: at Anqing and Nanyang rain from the fifth month to the seventh month flooded grain seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 4: rain from the fifth month to the seventh month at Anqing and Nanyang flooded grain seedlings.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，淮、鳳、揚、徐大雨，腐二麥。

translations.literal: Year 7, fifth month: at Huai, Feng, Yang, and Xu great rain rotted the second crop of wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 7, fifth month: great rain at Huai, Feng, Yang, and Xu rotted the second crop of wheat.

sentences.zh: 武昌、漢陽、荊州廬舍漂沒，民皆依山露宿。

translations.literal: At Wuchang, Hanyang, and Jingzhou dwellings were swept away and submerged; the people all camped in the open on the hills.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuchang, Hanyang, and Jingzhou dwellings were swept away and submerged; the people all camped in the open on the hills.

sentences.zh: 成化元年六月，畿東大雨，水壞山海關、永平、薊州、遵化城堡。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 1, sixth month: in the eastern metropolitan region great rain; water damaged the castles of Shanhai Pass, Yongping, Jizhou, and Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 1, sixth month: great rain in the eastern metropolitan region damaged the castles of Shanhai Pass, Yongping, Jizhou, and Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 八月，通州大雨，壞城及運倉。

translations.literal: Eighth month: at Tongzhou great rain damaged the city and transport granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: great rain at Tongzhou damaged the city and transport granaries.

sentences.zh: 二年，定州積雨，壞城垣及墩臺垛口百七十三。

translations.literal: Year 2: at Dingzhou accumulated rain damaged the city wall and one hundred seventy-three crenellations of beacon towers and parapets.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 2: accumulated rain at Dingzhou damaged the city wall and one hundred seventy-three crenellations of beacon towers and parapets.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，南京大風雨，壞天、地壇、孝陵廟宇。

translations.literal: Year 8, seventh month: at Nanjing great wind and rain damaged the altars of Heaven and Earth and the temples of the Xiaoling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 8, seventh month: great wind and rain at Nanjing damaged the altars of Heaven and Earth and the temples of the Xiaoling Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽大雨，壞皇陵牆垣。

translations.literal: At Fengyang great rain damaged the wall of the imperial mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengyang great rain damaged the wall of the imperial mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，南京大風雨，拔太廟、社稷壇樹。

translations.literal: Year 9, third month: at Nanjing great wind and rain uprooted the trees of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the altars of the soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 9, third month: great wind and rain at Nanjing uprooted the trees of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the altars of the soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 十三年七月，京城大雨。

translations.literal: Year 13, seventh month: at the capital great rain.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 13, seventh month: great rain at the capital.

sentences.zh: 十四年八月，鳳陽大雨，沒城內民居以千計。

translations.literal: Year 14, eighth month: at Fengyang great rain submerged commoners' dwellings within the city by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 14, eighth month: great rain at Fengyang submerged thousands of dwellings within the city.

sentences.zh: 十七年七月乙酉，南京大風雨，社稷壇及太廟殿宇皆摧。

translations.literal: Year 17, seventh month, day yiyou: at Nanjing great wind and rain; the altars of the soil and grain and the halls of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 17, seventh month, day yiyou: great wind and rain at Nanjing destroyed the altars of the soil and grain and the halls of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 十八年，河南、懷慶諸府，夏秋霪雨三月，塌城垣千一百八十餘丈，漂公署、壇廟、民居三十一萬四千間有奇，淹死一萬一千八百餘人。

translations.literal: Year 18: in Henan, Huaqing, and various prefectures, from summer to autumn incessant rain for three months collapsed more than one thousand one hundred eighty zhang of city walls, swept away more than three hundred fourteen thousand odd offices, altars, temples, and commoners' dwellings, and drowned more than eleven thousand eight hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 18: in Henan, Huaqing, and other prefectures incessant rain from summer to autumn for three months collapsed more than 1,180 zhang of city walls, swept away more than 314,000 government offices, altars, temples, and private dwellings, and drowned more than 11,800 people.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年七月，京師霪雨，求直言。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 2, seventh month: at the capital incessant rain; forthright remonstrance was sought.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 2, seventh month: incessant rain at the capital; the throne sought forthright remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，南京驟雨，壞午門西城壇。

translations.literal: Year 3, seventh month: at Nanjing sudden rain damaged the western altar outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 3, seventh month: sudden rain at Nanjing damaged the western altar outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 七年七月庚寅，南京大風雨，壞殿宇、城樓獸吻，拔太廟、天、地、社稷壇及孝陵樹。

translations.literal: Year 7, seventh month, day gengyin: at Nanjing great wind and rain damaged hall buildings and city-tower beast ornaments, uprooting the trees of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the altars of Heaven and Earth and the soil and grain, and the Xiaoling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 7, seventh month, day gengyin: great wind and rain at Nanjing damaged halls and city-tower beast ornaments and uprooted the trees of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the altars of Heaven, Earth, and the soil and grain, and the Xiaoling Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 自五月至八月，義州等衛連雨害稼。

translations.literal: From the fifth month to the eighth month, at Yizhou and other guards continuous rain harmed crops.
translations.idiomatic: From the fifth month to the eighth month continuous rain at Yizhou and other guards harmed crops.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，南京陰雨逾月，壞朝陽門北城堵。

translations.literal: Year 8, fifth month: at Nanjing overcast rain for more than a month damaged the northern parapet outside Chaoyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8, fifth month: overcast rain at Nanjing for more than a month damaged the northern parapet outside Chaoyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 九月，潮州諸府，颶風暴雨壞城垣廬舍。

translations.literal: Ninth month: in the various prefectures of Chaozhou hurricane and violent rain damaged city walls and dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: hurricane and violent rain in the prefectures of Chaozhou damaged city walls and dwellings.

sentences.zh: 十年七月，安陸霪雨，壞城郭廬舍殆盡。

translations.literal: Year 10, seventh month: at Anlu incessant rain; city walls and dwellings were nearly all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 10, seventh month: incessant rain at Anlu nearly destroyed all city walls and dwellings.

sentences.zh: 十一年七月，長安嶺暴風雨，壞城及廬舍。

translations.literal: Year 11, seventh month: at Chang'an Ridge violent wind and rain damaged the city and dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 11, seventh month: violent wind and rain at Chang'an Ridge damaged the city and dwellings.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月，義、錦、廣寧霪雨，壞城垣、墩堡、倉庫、橋樑，民多壓死者。

translations.literal: Year 14, sixth month: at Yi, Jin, and Guangning incessant rain damaged city walls, beacon forts, storehouses, and bridges; many commoners were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 14, sixth month: incessant rain at Yi, Jin, and Guangning damaged city walls, beacon forts, storehouses, and bridges; many commoners were crushed to death.

sentences.zh: 十五年六七月，南京大風雨，孝陵神宮監及懿文陵樹木、橋樑、牆垣多摧拔者。

translations.literal: Year 15, sixth and seventh months: at Nanjing great wind and rain; at the Xiaoling Spirit Palace Directorate and the Yiwen Mausoleum many trees, bridges, and walls were uprooted or destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 15, sixth and seventh months: great wind and rain at Nanjing uprooted or destroyed many trees, bridges, and walls at the Xiaoling Spirit Palace Directorate and the Yiwen Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 十六年五月，榆林大風雨，毀子城垣，移垣洞於其南五十步。

translations.literal: Year 16, fifth month: at Yulin great wind and rain destroyed the outer city wall and moved the wall opening fifty paces to its south.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 16, fifth month: great wind and rain at Yulin destroyed the outer city wall and shifted the wall opening fifty paces to the south.

sentences.zh: 十八年三月，雙山堡大雷雨壞城。

translations.literal: Year 18, third month: at Shuangshan Fort great thunder and rain damaged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 18, third month: great thunder and rain at Shuangshan Fort damaged the city.

sentences.zh: 六月至八月，京畿連雨。

translations.literal: From the sixth month to the eighth month, in the metropolitan region continuous rain.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth month to the eighth month the metropolitan region had continuous rain.

sentences.zh: 正德元年七月，鳳陽諸府大雨，平地水深丈五尺，沒居民五百餘家。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 1, seventh month: in the various prefectures of Fengyang great rain; water on level ground was one zhang five chi deep, submerging more than five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 1, seventh month: great rain in the prefectures of Fengyang left level ground one zhang five chi deep in water and submerged more than five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，武平大風雨，毀城樓。

translations.literal: Year 2, seventh month: at Wuping great wind and rain destroyed the city tower.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 2, seventh month: great wind and rain at Wuping destroyed the city tower.

sentences.zh: 長泰、南靖大風雨三日夜，平地水深二丈，漂民居八百餘家。

translations.literal: At Changtai and Nanjing great wind and rain for three days and nights; water on level ground was two zhang deep, sweeping away more than eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At Changtai and Nanjing great wind and rain for three days and nights left level ground two zhang deep in water and swept away more than eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十二年，蘇、鬆、常、鎮、嘉、湖大雨，殺麥禾。

translations.literal: Year 12: at Su, Song, Chang, Zhen, Jia, and Hu great rain killed wheat and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 12: great rain at Su, Song, Chang, Zhen, Jia, and Hu ruined wheat and grain.

sentences.zh: 十三年，應天、蘇、鬆、常、鎮、揚大雨彌月，漂室廬人畜無算。

translations.literal: Year 13: at Yingtian, Su, Song, Chang, Zhen, and Yang great rain for a full month swept away dwellings, livestock, and people beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 13: great rain for a full month at Yingtian, Su, Song, Chang, Zhen, and Yang swept away dwellings, livestock, and people beyond count.

sentences.zh: 十六年，京師久雨傷稼。

translations.literal: Year 16: at the capital prolonged rain harmed crops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 16: prolonged rain at the capital harmed crops.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年六月，登州大雨壞城。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 4, sixth month: at Dengzhou great rain damaged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 4, sixth month: great rain at Dengzhou damaged the city.

sentences.zh: 十六年，京師雨，自夏及秋不絕，房屋傾倒，軍民多壓死。

translations.literal: Year 16: at the capital rain from summer to autumn did not cease; houses collapsed and many soldiers and commoners were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 16: rain at the capital from summer to autumn did not cease; houses collapsed and many soldiers and commoners were crushed to death.

sentences.zh: 二十五年八月，京師大雨，壞九門城垣。

translations.literal: Year 25, eighth month: at the capital great rain damaged the city walls of the Nine Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 25, eighth month: great rain at the capital damaged the city walls of the Nine Gates.

sentences.zh: 三十三年六月，京師大雨，平地水數尺。

translations.literal: Year 33, sixth month: at the capital great rain; water on level ground was several chi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 33, sixth month: great rain at the capital left level ground several chi deep in water.

sentences.zh: 四十五年九月，鄖陽大霪雨，平地水丈餘。

translations.literal: Year 45, ninth month: at Yunyang great incessant rain; water on level ground was more than one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 45, ninth month: great incessant rain at Yunyang left level ground more than one zhang deep in water.

sentences.zh: 壞城垣廬舍，人民溺死無算。

translations.literal: City walls and dwellings were damaged; people drowned beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: City walls and dwellings were damaged, and people drowned beyond count.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年六月，京師霪雨，遼東自五月至七月雨不止，壞垣牆禾黍。

translations.literal: Longqing year 1, sixth month: at the capital incessant rain; in Liaodong from the fifth month to the seventh month rain did not stop, damaging walls and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing 1, sixth month: incessant rain at the capital; in Liaodong rain from the fifth month to the seventh month did not stop, damaging walls and grain.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年七月，霪雨。

translations.literal: Wanli year 1, seventh month: incessant rain.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 1, seventh month: incessant rain.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月，承天大雨水。

translations.literal: Year 11, fourth month: at Chengtian great rain water.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 11, fourth month: great rain at Chengtian.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，喜峯口大風雨，壞各墩臺。

translations.literal: Year 12, first month: at Xifeng Pass great wind and rain damaged the various beacon towers.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 12, first month: great wind and rain at Xifeng Pass damaged the various beacon towers.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月至七月，蘇、鬆諸府霪雨，禾麥俱傷。

translations.literal: Year 15, from the fifth month to the seventh month: at Su, Song, and various prefectures incessant rain; grain and wheat were both harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 15, fifth month to seventh month: incessant rain at Su, Song, and other prefectures harmed both grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 六月，京師大雨。

translations.literal: Sixth month: at the capital great rain.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: great rain at the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，杭、嘉、湖霪雨傷苗。

translations.literal: Year 24: at Hang, Jia, and Hu incessant rain harmed seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 24: incessant rain at Hang, Jia, and Hu harmed seedlings.

sentences.zh: 二十八年七月，興化、莆田、連江、福安大雨數日夜，城垣、橋樑、堤岸俱圮。

translations.literal: Year 28, seventh month: at Xinghua, Putian, Lianjiang, and Fu'an great rain for several days and nights; city walls, bridges, and dikes were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 28, seventh month: great rain for several days and nights at Xinghua, Putian, Lianjiang, and Fu'an destroyed city walls, bridges, and dikes.

sentences.zh: 二十九年春夏，蘇、鬆、嘉、湖霪雨傷麥。

translations.literal: Year 29, spring and summer: at Su, Song, Jia, and Hu incessant rain harmed wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 29, spring and summer: incessant rain at Su, Song, Jia, and Hu harmed wheat.

sentences.zh: 三十二年七月，京師霪雨，城崩。

translations.literal: Year 32, seventh month: at the capital incessant rain; the city collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 32, seventh month: incessant rain at the capital; the city wall collapsed.

sentences.zh: 三十三年五月丙申，鳳陽大風雨，損皇陵正殿御座。

translations.literal: Year 33, fifth month, day bingshen: at Fengyang great wind and rain damaged the imperial seat in the main hall of the imperial mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 33, fifth month, day bingshen: great wind and rain at Fengyang damaged the imperial seat in the main hall of the imperial mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 三十九年春，河南大雨。

translations.literal: Year 39, spring: at Henan great rain.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 39, spring: great rain in Henan.

sentences.zh: 夏，京師、廣東大雨。

translations.literal: Summer: at the capital and Guangdong great rain.
translations.idiomatic: Summer: great rain at the capital and in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 廣西積雨五閱月。

translations.literal: At Guangxi accumulated rain for five months.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangxi accumulated rain lasted five months.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，浙江霪雨爲災。

translations.literal: Year 42: in Zhejiang incessant rain became a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 42: incessant rain in Zhejiang became a disaster.

sentences.zh: 天啓六年閏六月，大雨連旬，壞天壽山神路，都城橋樑。

translations.literal: Tianqi year 6, intercalary sixth month: great rain for ten days in succession damaged the spirit road of Tianshou Mountain and the bridges of the capital city.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 6, intercalary sixth month: great rain for ten days in succession damaged the spirit road of Tianshou Mountain and the bridges of the capital.

sentences.zh: 是歲，遼東霪雨，壞山海關內外城垣，軍民傷者甚衆。

translations.literal: That year: in Liaodong incessant rain damaged the city walls inside and outside Shanhai Pass; soldiers and commoners harmed were very many.
translations.idiomatic: That year incessant rain in Liaodong damaged the city walls inside and outside Shanhai Pass, and very many soldiers and commoners were harmed.

sentences.zh: 七年，山東州縣二十有八積雨傷禾。

translations.literal: Year 7: in Shandong twenty-eight prefectures and counties accumulated rain harmed the grain crop.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 7: accumulated rain in twenty-eight prefectures and counties of Shandong harmed the grain crop.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年六月，大雨。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 5, sixth month: great rain.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 5, sixth month: great rain.

sentences.zh: 八月，又雨，衝損慶陵。

translations.literal: Eighth month: rain again; it damaged Qing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: rain fell again and damaged Qing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 九月，順天二十七縣霪雨害稼。

translations.literal: Ninth month: at Shuntian twenty-seven counties incessant rain harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: incessant rain in twenty-seven counties of Shuntian harmed the crops.

sentences.zh: 十一年夏，雨浹旬，圮南山邊垣。

translations.literal: Year 11, summer: rain for more than ten days; the southern mountain border wall collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 11, summer: rain lasted more than ten days and the southern mountain border wall collapsed.

sentences.zh: 十二年十二月，浙江霪雨，阡陌成巨浸。

translations.literal: Year 12, twelfth month: in Zhejiang incessant rain; fields and paths became a vast flood.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 12, twelfth month: incessant rain in Zhejiang turned fields and paths into a vast flood.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月至七月，寧、池諸郡霪雨，田半爲壑。

translations.literal: Year 13, fourth month to seventh month: at Ning and Chi and other prefectures incessant rain; half the fields became gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 13, fourth month to seventh month: incessant rain in Ning, Chi, and other prefectures turned half the fields into gullies.

sentences.zh: 十五年十月，黃、蘄、德安諸郡縣霪雨。

translations.literal: Year 15, tenth month: at Huang, Qi, and De'an and other prefectures and counties incessant rain.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 15, tenth month: incessant rain at Huang, Qi, De'an, and other prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 十六年二月戊辰，親祀社稷，大風雨，僅成禮而還。

translations.literal: Year 16, second month, day wuchen: the emperor personally sacrificed to the altars of soil and grain; great wind and rain; he barely completed the rites and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 16, second month, day wuchen: the emperor personally sacrificed at the altars of soil and grain amid great wind and rain, barely completing the rites before returning.

sentences.zh: ▲狂人

translations.literal: ▲ Madmen.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Madmen

sentences.zh: 景泰三年五月癸巳朔，以明日立太子，具香亭於奉天門。

translations.literal: Jingtai year 3, fifth month, new moon of day guisi: because the crown prince was to be installed the next day, incense pavilions were set up at Fengtian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 3, fifth month, new moon of day guisi: with the crown prince to be installed the next day, incense pavilions were set up at Fengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 有一人自外竟入，執紅棍擊香亭曰：「先打東方甲乙木。

translations.literal: A man from outside rushed straight in, seized a red staff, and struck the incense pavilion, saying: "First strike the eastern jia and yi wood."
translations.idiomatic: A man from outside rushed straight in, seized a red staff, struck the incense pavilion, and cried: "Strike the eastern jia and yi wood first!"

sentences.zh: 」嘉靖十八年，駕將南幸，有軍人孫堂從御路中橋至奉天門下，登金臺，坐久，守門官役無知者。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 18: as the imperial procession was about to travel south, the soldier Sun Tang went from the middle of the imperial route bridge to below Fengtian Gate, ascended the Golden Terrace, and sat for a long while; the gatekeepers and attendants knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 18: as the imperial procession was about to travel south, the soldier Sun Tang walked from the middle of the imperial route bridge to below Fengtian Gate, ascended the Golden Terrace, and sat for a long while while gatekeepers and attendants remained unaware.

sentences.zh: 升堂大呼，覺而捕之，乃病狂者。

translations.literal: He ascended the hall and shouted loudly; when they realized, they seized him—it was a man deranged by illness.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the hall and shouted loudly; once discovered he was seized—a man deranged by illness.

sentences.zh: ▲服妖

translations.literal: ▲ Garment omens.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Garment Omens

sentences.zh: 正德元年，婦女多用珠結蓋頭，謂之瓔珞。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 1: women widely used pearl-knotted veils, calling them yingluo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 1: women widely wore pearl-knotted veils called yingluo.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，車駕還京，令朝臣用曳撒大帽鸞帶。

translations.literal: Year 13, first month: when the imperial procession returned to the capital, court officials were ordered to use yisan, large hats, and luan belts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 13, first month: when the imperial procession returned to the capital, court officials were ordered to wear yisan, large hats, and luan belts.

sentences.zh: 給事中硃鳴陽言，曳撒大帽，行役所用，非見君服。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhu Mingyang said that yisan and large hats were what runners and laborers used—not attire for appearing before the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhu Mingyang protested that yisan and large hats were attire for runners and laborers, not for appearing before the ruler.

sentences.zh: 皆近服妖也。

translations.literal: All were near to garment omens.
translations.idiomatic: All were regarded as near to garment omens.

sentences.zh: 十五年十二月，帝平宸濠還京，俘從逆者及懸諸逆首於竿，皆標以白幟，數里皆白。

translations.literal: Year 15, twelfth month: when the emperor pacified Prince Ning's rebellion and returned to the capital, captives who had followed the rebellion and the rebel leaders hung on poles were all marked with white banners; for several li everything was white.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 15, twelfth month: when the emperor pacified the Prince of Ning's rebellion and returned to the capital, captives who had followed the rebellion and rebel leaders hung on poles were all marked with white banners, and for several li everything was white.

sentences.zh: 時帝已不豫，見者識其不祥。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was already unwell; those who saw it recognized its ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already unwell at the time, and onlookers recognized the ill omen.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，朝臣好以紗縠、竹籜爲帶，取其便易。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen era court officials liked to use gauze, fine silk, and bamboo splints as belts, taking them for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era court officials favored gauze, fine silk, and bamboo splints as belts for their convenience.

sentences.zh: 論者謂金銀重而貴，紗籜賤而輕，殆賤將乘貴也。

translations.literal: Commentators said gold and silver were heavy and noble, while gauze and splints were base and light—perhaps the base would overcome the noble.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said gold and silver were heavy and noble while gauze and splints were base and light—perhaps the base would overcome the noble.

sentences.zh: 時北方小民制幘，低側其檐，自掩眉目，名曰：「不認親」。

translations.literal: At the time northern commoners made caps, lowering the brim to one side to cover their eyes and brows, calling them "won't recognize kin."
translations.idiomatic: At the time northern commoners made caps with brims lowered to one side to cover their eyes and brows, calling them "won't recognize kin."

sentences.zh: 其後寇亂民散，途遇親戚，有飲泣不敢言，或掉臂去之者。

translations.literal: Afterward when bandit turmoil scattered the people, meeting kin on the road some wept and dared not speak, or swung their arms and left.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, when bandit turmoil scattered the people, some who met kin on the road wept and dared not speak, or swung their arms and walked away.

sentences.zh: ▲雞禍

translations.literal: ▲ Chicken calamities.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Chicken Calamities

sentences.zh: 弘治十四年，華容民劉福家雞雛三足。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 14: at Huarong the commoner Liu Fu's household hen hatched a chick with three legs.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 14: at Huarong the commoner Liu Fu's household hen hatched a chick with three legs.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月，崇明民顧孟文家雞生雛，猴頭而人形，身長四寸，有尾，活動無聲。

translations.literal: Year 17, sixth month: at Chongming the commoner Gu Mengwen's household hen hatched a chick with a monkey's head and human form, four cun long, with a tail, active and soundless.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 17, sixth month: at Chongming the commoner Gu Mengwen's household hen hatched a chick with a monkey's head and human form, four cun long, with a tail, active yet soundless.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年，長垣民王憲家雞抱卵，內成人形，耳目口鼻四肢皆具。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 4: at Changyuan the commoner Wang Xian's household hen brooded an egg; inside was a human form with ears, eyes, mouth, nose, and all four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 4: at Changyuan the commoner Wang Xian's household hen brooded an egg containing a human form with ears, eyes, mouth, nose, and all four limbs.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十二年六月，靖邊營軍家雌雞化爲雄。

translations.literal: Wanli year 22, sixth month: at Jingbian Garrison a soldier's household hen transformed into a rooster.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 22, sixth month: at Jingbian Garrison a soldier's household hen transformed into a rooster.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年，淮安民家牝雞啼躍，化爲雄。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 9: at Huai'an a commoner's household hen crowed and leaped, transforming into a rooster.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 9: at Huai'an a commoner's household hen crowed and leaped, transforming into a rooster.

sentences.zh: 十年，宣武門外民家白雞，喙距純赤，重四十斤。

translations.literal: Year 10: outside Xuanwu Gate a commoner's household white hen had beak and spurs wholly red, weighing forty jin.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 10: outside Xuanwu Gate a commoner's household white hen had a wholly red beak and spurs and weighed forty jin.

sentences.zh: 或曰此皦也，所見之處國亡。

translations.literal: Some said this was the jiao; wherever it is seen the state perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Some said this was the jiao bird; wherever it appears the state perishes.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太倉衛指揮姜周輔家雞伏子，兩頭四翼八足。

translations.literal: Year 14: at Taicang Guard Commander Jiang Zhoufu's household a hen brooded chicks with two heads, four wings, and eight feet.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 14: at Taicang Guard Commander Jiang Zhoufu's household a hen brooded chicks with two heads, four wings, and eight feet.

sentences.zh: ▲鼠妖

translations.literal: ▲ Rat omens.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Rat Omens

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十四年七月，常、鎮、淮、揚諸郡，土鼠千萬成羣，夜銜尾渡江，絡繹不絕，幾一月方止。

translations.literal: Wanli year 44, seventh month: in Chang, Zhen, Huai, and Yang and other prefectures, earth rats in tens of millions formed groups; at night they bit one another's tails and crossed the river in an unbroken stream for nearly a month before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 44, seventh month: in Chang, Zhen, Huai, Yang, and other prefectures earth rats in tens of millions formed groups that at night bit one another's tails and crossed the river in an unbroken stream for nearly a month before stopping.

sentences.zh: 四十五年五月，南京有鼠萬餘，銜尾渡江，食禾稼。

translations.literal: Year 45, fifth month: at Nanjing more than ten thousand rats bit tails and crossed the river, eating grain crops.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 45, fifth month: at Nanjing more than ten thousand rats bit one another's tails and crossed the river, devouring the grain crops.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年，寧夏鼠十餘萬，銜尾食苗。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 7: at Ningxia more than one hundred thousand rats bit tails and ate seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 7: at Ningxia more than one hundred thousand rats bit one another's tails and ate the seedlings.

sentences.zh: 十二年，黃州鼠食禾，渡江五六日不絕。

translations.literal: Year 12: at Huangzhou rats ate the grain; crossing the river for five or six days without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 12: at Huangzhou rats ate the grain crops, crossing the river for five or six days without cease.

sentences.zh: 時內殿奏章房多鼠盜食，與人相觸而不畏，亦鼠妖也。

translations.literal: At the time in the inner palace memorial office there were many rats stealing food; they touched people without fear—also rat omens.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many rats in the inner palace memorial office stole food and touched people without fear—also rat omens.

sentences.zh: 至甲申元旦後，鼠始屏跡。

translations.literal: By the New Year's Day after jiashen the rats at last vanished.
translations.idiomatic: By the New Year's Day after the jiashen year the rats at last vanished.

sentences.zh: 又秦州關山中鼠化鵪鶉者以數千計。

translations.literal: Also in the passes and mountains of Qinzhou rats transformed into quail in numbers of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Also in the passes and mountains of Qinzhou rats transformed into quail in numbers of thousands.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，羣鼠渡江，晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: Year 15, second month: groups of rats crossed the river day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 15, second month: groups of rats crossed the river day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 十月，榆林、定邊諸堡鼠生蝦蟆腹中，一生數十，食苗如割。

translations.literal: Tenth month: at Yulin, Dingbian, and other forts rats were born in toads' bellies, several tens from one birth, eating seedlings as if reaped.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 15, tenth month: at Yulin, Dingbian, and other forts rats were born in toads' bellies, several tens from one birth, eating seedlings as if reaped.

sentences.zh: ▲木冰

translations.literal: ▲ Tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Tree Ice

sentences.zh: 洪武四年正月戊申，木冰。

translations.literal: Hongwu year 4, first month, day wushen: tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 4, first month, day wushen: tree ice.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月乙丑，雨木冰。

translations.literal: Year 6, twelfth month, day yichou: rain tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 6, twelfth month, day yichou: freezing rain coated the trees with ice.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月丁亥，雨木冰。

translations.literal: Year 11, first month, day dinghai: rain tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 11, first month, day dinghai: freezing rain coated the trees with ice.

sentences.zh: 二十二年正月甲戌，雨木冰。

translations.literal: Year 22, first month, day jiaxu: rain tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 22, first month, day jiaxu: freezing rain coated the trees with ice.

sentences.zh: 正統三年十月丁丑曉，木介。

translations.literal: Zhengtong year 3, tenth month, day dingchou, dawn: tree armor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 3, tenth month, day dingchou, at dawn: tree armor ice.

sentences.zh: 天順七年十月甲辰，雨木冰。

translations.literal: Tianshun year 7, tenth month, day jiachen: rain tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 7, tenth month, day jiachen: freezing rain coated the trees with ice.

sentences.zh: 八年正月乙丑，雨木冰。

translations.literal: Year 8, first month, day yichou: rain tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 8, first month, day yichou: freezing rain coated the trees with ice.

sentences.zh: 成化十六年正月辛卯曉，雨木冰。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 16, first month, day xinmao, dawn: rain tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 16, first month, day xinmao, at dawn: freezing rain coated the trees with ice.

sentences.zh: 二十三年十二月戊辰曉，木介。

translations.literal: Year 23, twelfth month, day wuchen, dawn: tree armor.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 23, twelfth month, day wuchen, at dawn: tree armor ice.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年十一月癸巳，木冰。

translations.literal: Longqing year 3, eleventh month, day guisi: tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing 3, eleventh month, day guisi: tree ice.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十四年冬，蘇、松木冰。

translations.literal: Wanli year 14, winter: at Su and Song tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 14, winter: tree ice at Su and Song.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年十一月，陝西木冰，樹枝盡折。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 1, eleventh month: in Shaanxi tree ice; tree branches all broke.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 1, eleventh month: tree ice in Shaanxi broke all the tree branches.

sentences.zh: 其後大河以北，歲有此異。

translations.literal: Afterward north of the Great River every year had this anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward this anomaly occurred every year north of the Great River.

sentences.zh: ▲木妖

translations.literal: ▲ Wood omens.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Wood Omens

sentences.zh: 弘治八年，長沙楓生李實，黃蓮生黃瓜。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 8: at Changsha a maple bore plums; a yellow lotus bore cucumbers.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8: at Changsha a maple bore plums and a yellow lotus bore cucumbers.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，長寧楠生蓮花，李生豆莢。

translations.literal: Year 9, third month: at Changning a nan tree bore lotus flowers; a plum bore bean pods.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 9, third month: at Changning a nan tree bore lotus flowers and a plum bore bean pods.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十七年十月戊辰，泗水沙中涌出大杉木，圍丈五尺，長六丈餘。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 37, tenth month, day wuchen: at Sishui a great fir emerged from the sand, circumference one zhang five chi, length more than six zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 37, tenth month, day wuchen: at Sishui a great fir emerged from the sand, one zhang five chi in circumference and more than six zhang long.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年四月，杭州慄生桃。

translations.literal: Longqing year 5, fourth month: at Hangzhou chestnut trees bore peaches.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing 5, fourth month: at Hangzhou chestnut trees bore peaches.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十八年五月丁卯，祖陵大松樹孔中吐火，竟日方滅。

translations.literal: Wanli year 18, fifth month, day dingmao: at the Imperial Ancestral Mausoleum a great pine tree spat fire from a hole and did not cease until day's end.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 18, fifth month, day dingmao: at the Imperial Ancestral Mausoleum a great pine tree spat fire from a hole and burned until day's end.

sentences.zh: 二十三年十二月癸亥，皇陵樹顛火出，延燒草木。

translations.literal: Year 23, twelfth month, day guihai: at the Imperial Mausoleum fire issued from the tops of trees and spread to burn grass and wood.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 23, twelfth month, day guihai: at the Imperial Mausoleum fire issued from the tops of trees and spread to burn grass and wood.

sentences.zh: 天啓六年四月癸巳，白露著樹如垂綿，日中不散。

translations.literal: Tianqi year 6, fourth month, day guisi: white dew clung to trees like hanging silk and did not disperse at midday.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 6, fourth month, day guisi: white dew clung to trees like hanging silk and did not disperse at midday.

sentences.zh: 十月辛酉，南京西華門內有煙無火。

translations.literal: Tenth month, day xinyou: inside the Xihua Gate at Nanjing there was smoke without fire.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 6, tenth month, day xinyou: inside the Xihua Gate at Nanjing there was smoke without fire.

sentences.zh: 禮臣往視，乃舊宮材木，瘞土中久，煙自生，土石皆焦。

translations.literal: Ritual officials went to inspect; it was old palace timber long buried in the earth, and smoke arose of itself; earth and stone were all scorched.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials inspected it and found old palace timber long buried in the earth, from which smoke arose of itself; earth and stone were all scorched.

sentences.zh: 以水沃之，三日始滅。

translations.literal: Water poured on it; only after three days did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: Water was poured on it, yet only after three days did it cease.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年五月癸巳，霍山縣有木甑飛墮，不知所自來。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 6, fifth month, day guisi: at Huoshan County a wooden steamer flew down; no one knew whence it came.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 6, fifth month, day guisi: at Huoshan County a wooden steamer flew down from nowhere known.

sentences.zh: 七年二月丁巳，太康門牡自開者三，知縣集邑紳議其事，樑墮而死。

translations.literal: Year 7, second month, day dingsi: at Taikang the gate bolt opened itself three times; the magistrate gathered local gentry to discuss the matter, and a beam fell and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 7, second month, day dingsi: at Taikang the gate bolt opened itself three times; the magistrate gathered local gentry to discuss the matter, and a beam fell and killed him.

sentences.zh: ▲青眚青祥

translations.literal: ▲ Blue afflictions and blue auspices.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Blue Afflictions and Blue Auspices

sentences.zh: 宣德元年八月辛巳，東南天有青氣，狀如人叉手揖拜。

translations.literal: Xuande year 1, eighth month, day xinsi: in the southeast sky there was blue qi, shaped like a person with hands clasped in salute.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande 1, eighth month, day xinsi: blue qi in the southeast sky was shaped like a person with hands clasped in salute.
